acceptanceCriteria: A test reproduces a pending redo held across several heartbeat calls on a live attempt and shows the heartbeat either completes the pending redo itself or returns within a documented bound shorter than the heartbeat TTL.
GitHub beamfall/corvint#860 questions 1 and 2 are answered in the spec text and the PR body.

While heartbeats are refused REDO_PENDING the attempt is not reaped or fenced on liveness grounds (TTL honoured or extended), proven by a test, or the result states explicitly (retryAfter / liveness-honoured field) whether liveness is preserved; the Tasks spec and help document which writer completes a pending redo and the caller contract.
body: Source: GitHub beamfall/corvint#860 (2026-10-13). `corvint-tasks attempt heartbeat` returned ERROR [REDO_PENDING] (retryable) on 5 consecutive calls 360 s apart (~18 min) on a native canonical-writer queue (writeBarrier NONE, ~37k receipts, 2-4 live attempts, no dispatcher). A caller treating three misses as lost (600 s TTL) fenced and killed a healthy 36-minute command. A later claim succeeded within ~6 min and queue status showed no pending redo. Expected: REDO_PENDING resolves within a bounded documented time shorter than the heartbeat TTL (e.g. the heartbeat writer completes the redo), or the result tells the caller how long to wait and whether liveness is honoured. Questions: what leaves a redo pending and which writer completes it; is the heartbeat TTL extended while heartbeats are refused. Code: internal/tasks (journal, snapshot/probe.go, cli). Related completed: V1-0648, V1-1126, V1-0309, V1-0780.
title: corvint-tasks attempt heartbeat refused REDO_PENDING for ~18 min fences a live attempt (GitHub #860)
